title: Quarterbacking Solo KPI Sprint Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Solo sprint notebook: keep a tight loop on personal KPI progress for the next 2 weeks, log fast experiments, and surface anything to the team at sync. Try to be pragmatic: 1 actionable decision per day.

Top-level objective (Northstar):
- Reduce average 95th-percentile token latency for small-chat workload by 12% while keeping infer-cost per 1k tokens within current budget band.

This sprint (2 weeks) success criteria:
- Target: p95 latency down ~10–14% vs baseline (baseline p95=210ms)
- Cost: <= +3% delta on per-1k-token unit cost (baseline $0.018 / 1k tokens)
- No regressions in quality > 2% on the reply-coverage eval set (quick A/B)

Metrics dashboard snapshot (manual pull, 2024-11-04):
- Baseline p50/p95/p99: 56ms / 210ms / 420ms
- QPS (small-chat): 450–520 (peak 680 last Tue)
- Cache hit rate (prefix KV): 28% overall, 41% for steady-state users
- Unit cost (hosted): $0.0178 / 1k tokens average last 7d

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Continuous batching policy tweak (smaller max delay + adaptive window) will reduce p95 without materially increasing cost.
   - Experiment: change batch window from 12ms->8ms, enable dynamic shrink if qps<120.
   - Metric: p95, mean batch size, token cost.

2) Aggressive KV prefix reuse for small messages: extend retention TTL on hot prefixes to 6s for identified cohorts.
   - Risk: memory pressure; need SRE guardrails.

3) Micro-quantization profile on embeddings step for rerankers (CPU fallback) to shave 5–6ms tail.
   - Need to validate quality delta on sample set.

Weekly plan (day-by-day):
- Mon (11/4): baseline harvest + confirm reproducibility; open PR for batching config change; smoke runs on staging by EOD.
- Tue (11/5): run 4x load tests across peak shapes; instrument trace-level p95 buckets; check mem/cpu.
- Wed (11/6): enable adaptive window in canary on dedicated pool (10% traffic). Triage anomalies.
- Thu (11/7): evaluate results; if p95 improved >=8% and no quality hit, roll to 50% canary; otherwise revert and log learnings.
- Fri (11/8): write mini-retro + next-steps; plan KV TTL experiment for next sprint.

Action items (owner = me unless listed):
- A1: open PR for batching config and add unit tests for window logic (blocked by infra test harness flakiness) — target: 11/4 — status: in progress.
- A2: add p95/trace instrumentation to perf dashboard + alert on >10% regression — target: 11/5 — status: done (basic).
- A3: coordinate with SRE to carve canary pool and allocate mem headroom for KV TTL test — target: 11/6 — collaborator: Jordan Hayes.
- A4: prepare short eval script to run quality checks on 500 prompts for reranker quantization — target: 11/7 — collaborator: Priya Menon.
- A5: write post-mortem template for any rollout regressions (one-pager) — target: 11/8 — status: draft.

Quick retro notes (end of week 1):
- Wins:
  - Baseline harvesting was fast; raw metrics aligned with expectations.
  - Dashboard instrumentation gave better visibility into which request paths drive tail.
- Frictions:
  - Test harness flaked intermittently (timeouts), slowed PR validation. Need to file infra ticket.
  - Hard to attribute cost change to a single factor when multiple small config changes land simultaneously.
- Decisions:
  - Keep adaptive window turned on for canary, but cap max batch size at 64 to limit latency spikes.

Personal habit experiment (meta-KPI):
- Goal: ship one small perf change every 72 hours during this sprint (smaller loop).
- Habit: morning 30-min spike to unblock infra; evening 15-min doc update and checklist completion.
- Check-ins: log completion each day in this doc (quick ticks).

Risks & blockers:
- Memory growth if KV TTL increased; mitigation: set hard eviction threshold and alert to SRE.
- If load shapes vary dramatically, canary signals may be noisy. Will increase sample size.

Open questions (to resolve quickly):
- What is the minimum effective cache TTL that yields >5% p95 improvement? Need small grid search.
- Can we tighten SLA with dedicated infra for small-chat without incurring 2–3x cost? (talk to product)

Notes-to-self (brain dump):
- Keep propositions 1–2 short. If early signals negative, cut and pivot to KV experiment.
- Avoid making >1 change in prod at same time; keep experiments orthogonal.
- When writing PR, include a short 'how to revert' section so on-call can revert quickly.

Follow-ups for next retro (11/18):
- Full boarding summary: p95 delta, cost delta, quality delta, canary decisions.
- Clean up telemetry noise: remove duplicate spans from grpc layer.
- Post any infra flakiness tickets with root cause and owner.

References / quick links:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/709
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4821 (batching policy work)
- Notes: confluence:ops/kv-cache-notes (fragile, add summary)

Daily ticks (progress tracker):
- 2024-11-04: A1 started, baseline harvest complete, dashboard added.
- 2024-11-05: Load tests run; trace buckets look clean; harness timeouts observed.
- 2024-11-06: Canary 10% deployed with adaptive window; no immediate regressions.

End of doc: leave this as a living notebook; prune into a concise retro and a single PR summary after sprint close.
